summary: The game is a 2D simulator about administrating a spacial base, made for one player and for computers. In the game there's a part that says "Base Status" in which there are six parameters: "Oxygen", "Water", "Food", "Electricity", "Radiation Shield" and "Morale". These parameters have to be above a certain level so the mission can go on without any issues and the astronauts can get back home safe.
details:
Project Summary: NASA Space Mission Simulator (Team AstroUy) Challenge: Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer

NASA Space Mission Simulator is an interactive space habitat management game built with Rosebud AI where players manage a 10-day survival mission on either the Moon or Mars. Designed as a training tool for future astronauts, the simulator challenges players to balance six critical survival metrics—Oxygen, Water, Food, Electricity, Radiation Shielding, and Crew Morale—while managing a 3-member crew and limited mission credits.

Current Playable Prototype (MVP): The web prototype features both Lunar and Martian environments with a real-time Base Status HUD, 5 constructible modules (Solar Array, Greenhouse, Habitat, Ice Extractor, and Radiation Bunker), a functional Research Lab for permanent upgrades using Research Points, an Earth Supply Channel with 48-hour cargo transit delays, and a time-advancement system (+3h) that triggers 7 random decision-making events (such as Solar Flares, Micrometeorite Impacts, Crop Blight, and Dust Fronts).

Planned Expansion & NASA Science Integration: To deepen educational realism, our Game Design Document (GDD) outlines the next update using real datasets from NASA’s Planetary Fact Sheets, LRO, Mars MEDA, Artemis, and Perseverance (MOXIE). This update introduces distinct planetary pros and cons—such as faster Earth resupplies (24h) and 100% peak solar irradiance (1361 W/m2) vs. 14-day lunar nights and extreme radiation on the Moon, compared to atmospheric CO2 oxygen generation vs. 48–72h resupply delays and solar-blocking dust storms on Mars—alongside an individual Crew Energy system that directly impacts daily base productivity.

What Our Game Brings (Educational and Strategic Value):

  • Realistic Astronaut Training: Translates real NASA planetary science into interactive survival mechanics, teaching players how to manage a 10-day habitat mission on the Moon or Mars.
  • Critical Thinking and Crisis Management: Challenges players to balance 6 vital resources (Oxygen, Water, Food, Electricity, Radiation Shielding, and Crew Morale) while reacting to 7 random decision events every 3 hours.
  • Comparative Planetary Science: Highlights the real-world pros and cons of lunar vs. martian colonization (such as faster Earth resupplies and 100% peak solar efficiency vs. extreme radiation on the Moon, compared to atmospheric CO2 oxygen generation vs. dust storms and 48-hour transit delays on Mars).

Tools and NASA Resources Used:

  • Rosebud AI: Used to build the playable web prototype, 2D planetary environments, interactive UI panels (Base Status, Earth Supply Channel, Research Lab), and core JavaScript/WebGL logic.
  • NASA Datasets and Missions: NASA Planetary Fact Sheets (gravity, escape velocity, solar irradiance, and Bond albedo), LRO Diviner, Mars MEDA, Artemis program, and Perseverance MOXIE.
  • Documentation Tools: Google Docs and Google Slides for the Game Design Document (GDD) and the 7-slide mission presentation.
